responses:
I fixed the failing test and committed it as `4da6726` on `feat/quote-pdf`, but **the Arabic font file itself isn't in the repo yet**, so real Arabic PDFs still won't use it.

**Cause:** The test was correct. The feature just hadn't been built: the template never added an `@font-face` rule for Arabic quotes. ADR-0007 requires the font to be embedded from `app/fonts/` rather than taken from the system.

**Fix** (`app/pdf.py`):
- Arabic quotes now get a `<style>` block with an `@font-face` rule pointing at `app/fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf`, and the page text uses that font.
- English quotes are unchanged.

**Tests** (`tests/test_rtl_font.py`): The original check is unchanged. I removed its outdated "not implemented yet" comment and added two tests: one checks the font is loaded from `app/fonts/`, and one checks English quotes don't get the Arabic font. All 12 tests pass.

**About the missing font:** `app/fonts/` doesn't exist. The HTML now points at the right file, but until the `.ttf` is added, WeasyPrint will fall back to a system font when it renders, which is what the ADR rules out. I couldn't download a font file here. Noto Naskh Arabic is free to bundle (SIL Open Font License). If you'd rather use a different font, it's a one-line change to `ARABIC_FONT_FILE`. If you want, I can also make rendering fail loudly when the font file is missing, so it can't silently fall back.
